title: Transformers
subtitle: Module 9 · T1 Chapter 11 · encoder and decoder blocks, parameters, ViT, the three Transformer families and fine-tuning

lesson.title: Why Transformers?
lesson.lead: "Attention is all you need" (2017): drop recurrence and let every token attend to every other token **in parallel**.

blocks.text: Impact: translation (2017) → BERT (2018) → GPT series → today's LLMs (100B+ parameters), small models for on-device use (1–7B), ViT and CLIP for vision, Whisper for speech, and multimodal models.

lesson.title: The encoder block
lesson.lead: Embedding + position → [**multi-head attention → add & norm → FFN → add & norm**] × N.

blocks.text: X = Embedding(tokens) + PE(positions)      E ∈ R^{|V| × d_model}
Z₁ = X + MHA(LayerNorm(X))        Z₂ = Z₁ + FFN(LayerNorm(Z₁))
blocks.caption: the deck's pre-norm form

head: Sub-layer
What it does
rows: Tokens "communicate": headₕ = softmax(QₕKₕᵀ/√d_k)Vₕ; e.g. H = 12, d_k = D/H = 64
Each token "thinks" alone: D → 4D → D with ReLU (GELU in ViT); same weights at every position
LN(x) = γ(x − E[x])/√(Var[x] + ε) + β over features, not the batch; the same at train and test
out = x + sublayer(x): gradient highways (from ResNet) for 100+ layers

blocks.text: The encoder is **bidirectional**: every token sees all others ("bank" in "river bank" vs "bank account"). Stacks: original N = 6, BERT-base 12, BERT-large 24.

lesson.title: The decoder block
lesson.lead: Three sub-layers: **masked self-attention → cross-attention to the encoder → FFN**.

blocks.text: Z₁ = Y + MaskedMHA(LN(Y))    Z₂ = Z₁ + CrossAttn(LN(Z₁), H_enc)    Z₃ = Z₂ + FFN(LN(Z₂))

items: **Masked** self-attention: token t sees only positions ≤ t, so training matches token-by-token generation.
**Cross-attention**: Q from the decoder, K and V from the encoder output H_enc; no mask over source tokens.
Output: logits = D W_out + b (W_out is d_model × |V|) → softmax → pick a token (greedy, sampling, or beam search).

blocks.text: Training uses teacher forcing: all target positions are predicted in parallel under the mask. Inference generates one token at a time: ⟨s⟩ → "yeh" → "kitab" → …

lesson.title: Counting parameters
lesson.lead: Per layer the deck counts ≈ **12 d_model²** for an encoder and ≈ **16 d_model²** for a decoder.

head: Part
Encoder layer
Decoder layer
rows: Attention projections W^Q, W^K, W^V, W^O

blocks.text: With d_model = 512: encoder layer ≈ 12 × 512² = **3,145,728**; decoder layer ≈ 16 × 512² = **4,194,304** (biases ignored). Embeddings add |V| × d_model (30K–50K tokens × 512).

blocks.label: Common slip
blocks.text: Multi-head attention does **not** multiply parameters by h: each head uses d_k = d_model/h, so the four projection matrices are still d_model × d_model in total.

lesson.title: Vision Transformer (ViT)
lesson.lead: Cut the image into **patches**, treat them as tokens, and use an encoder-only Transformer.

blocks.text: N = HW / P² = 224·224 / 16² = 196 patches;  each patch 16·16·3 = 768 values → linear projection Wₚ ∈ R^{(P²C)×d}

items: L encoder layers (ViT-Base: L = 12, H = 12, d_k = 64, FFN with GELU).
Classify from the [CLS] output: LayerNorm → W_head (d × K) → softmax.

head: CNN
ViT
rows: Quadratic in the number of patches

blocks.text: Use CNNs for < 100K images or little compute; ViT when large pre-training is available; hybrids put a CNN stem under a Transformer body.

blocks.label: Exam rule
blocks.text: Selection guide: classify or extract → encoder-only; generate text → decoder-only; input and output very different (another language, a summary) → encoder–decoder.
NER example (encoder-only): "Teddy was US President" → [PER, O, LOC, O]. Completion (decoder-only): "The weather today is" → "sunny and warm…".

lesson.title: Pre-training and fine-tuning
lesson.lead: Pre-train on huge unlabelled text, then **fine-tune** on 1K–100K labelled examples.

items: Load a pre-trained model and tokenizer (e.g. bert-base-uncased from Hugging Face).
Tokenise the task data with the same tokenizer; split train/validation.
Fine-tune with a **small learning rate** (2e-5 to 5e-5), **2–5 epochs**, AdamW with weight decay 0.01, batch 16–32, gradient clipping at 1.0.

head: Approach
What is trained
rows: < 1% of parameters: W = W_frozen + α·BA, B ∈ R^{d×r}, A ∈ R^{r×d}, r ≪ d

lesson.title: Exam angles
lesson.lead: Expect dimension bookkeeping, "why scale by √d_k", and design trade-offs.

blocks.text: **Heads vs width (EC-3 2026 Q4c):** raising d_model gives one richer attention pattern per layer but costs O(d²) more parameters and compute and can overfit. More heads (same d_model) cost the same parameters but let different heads specialise in different relations (syntax, coreference, position). Many heads of d_k = d_model/h learn diverse, complementary subspaces; one big head averages them into a single pattern.

**Missing scaling (EC-3 2026 Q4b):** with d_k = 512 and no 1/√d_k, dot products have variance ≈ d_k, so scores exceed 100. Softmax becomes one-hot, its Jacobian diag(p) − ppᵀ ≈ 0, and learning stalls.

**W^Q, W^K, W^V shapes (EC-3 makeup 2023 Q2):** with input d, query size d_q, key/value sizes d_k, d_v and h heads, the per-head projections are d × d_q, d × d_k, d × d_v; stacked over heads (h·d) × d_q etc.; W^O is (h·d_v) × d. Stacked over 6 heads: W^Q = (6 × 1024) × 256, W^K = W^V = (6 × 1024) × 512, W^O = (6 × 512) × 1024.

worked.title: Scaled score for one query and one key (EC-3 2026 Q4)

steps.label: Softmax
steps.text: With a single key the weight is 1 whatever the score, so the output is V = (1, 3).

steps.label: Why scaling matters
steps.text: With many keys, dividing by √d_k shrinks gaps between scores, so softmax stays soft and gradients flow. Without it, large d_k gives near one-hot weights and vanishing gradients.

worked.title: Encoder and decoder layer parameters

problem.text: d_model = 512, d_ff = 4d_model. Estimate the parameters of one encoder layer and one decoder layer (ignore biases).

worked.answer: ≈ 3.1M per encoder layer, ≈ 4.2M per decoder layer.

problem.text: A 224 × 224 × 3 image with 16 × 16 patches and d = 768. How many tokens enter the encoder, and what is the shape of Wₚ and E_pos?

worked.title: Multi-head projection shapes (EC-3 makeup 2023 Q2)

problem.text: Input/attention dimension 1024, query dimension 256, key and value dimensions 512, 6 heads. Give W^Q, W^K, W^V, W^O and the attention vector size.

worked.answer: Attention vector after concatenation: 6 × 512 = 3072; W^O maps 3072 → 1024.
